name: fateful-tissue
title: Fateful tissue: a dividing tyssue whose divisions are decided by each cell's own metabolism→fate chain

behavior_tests.name: fate-drives-division
behavior_tests.description: The tissue carries out at least one fate-driven division over the run (emitted cumulative n_divisions ends >= 1) — biology, not a clock, divides the tissue.

behavior_tests.name: tissue-sustains
behavior_tests.description: The tissue does not collapse: the minimum simulated cell count stays at or above the initial 4 cells (growth keeps pace with division).

limitations: Sustained growth is a TUNED regime — target area tracks the metabolite so daughters regrow; without that coupling the vertex backend halves cells on division and the tissue collapses. The growth is engineered, not emergent.
Division is capped (max_divisions_per_step) and the divider is shuffled for tyssue stability; the exact lineage tree is not a controlled observable.
Particle conservation across splits is checked as 'particles survive' (n > 0), not yet as an exact mother == sum(daughters) count band.
claim: Every scale this workspace can simulate composes into one system: a tyssue of dividing cells, each running a Smoldyn particle sim confined to its moving polygon (split on division) AND an ODE metabolism whose metabolite pins a MaBoSS fate network — and the fate 'divide' output DRIVES the tissue division. Cells grow as they metabolise (target area tracks the metabolite), divide when their own fate fires, and daughters reset and regrow, so the tissue sustains. Biology decides when the tissue divides.
experiment: Run fateful_tissue (vertex backend) for 22 steps. Each step: advance every cell's confined particles and coupled metabolism→fate; divide the cells whose fate raised 'divide'; split the mother's particles into the daughters; grow each cell's target area with its metabolite.
outcomes: The fate-coloured flipbook (viz/fateful-tissue.html) shows the tissue growing from 4 to ~26 cells over ~22 fate-driven divisions, with particle counts conserved across each split and cell fill reading the metabolism→fate state (green metabolising → amber building → red dividing). Computed live from real tellurium + MaBoSS + Smoldyn.

question: Can a dividing tissue's divisions be decided by each cell's own metabolism->fate chain, with confined particles that split on division — composing every scale at once?

study_card.goal: Show that a dividing tissue's divisions can be decided by each cell's own metabolism->fate chain, composing all scales at once.
study_card.mechanism: A dividing tyssue where each cell runs confined Smoldyn particles (split on division) AND an ODE metabolism whose metabolite pins a MaBoSS fate network, and the fate 'divide' output drives the tissue division. Cells grow as they metabolise, divide when their own fate fires, and daughters reset and regrow.
study_card.why_before_next: The crown: it closes the loop from sub-cellular coupling back to tissue mechanics, showing biology (a cell's own fate chain) — not a clock — can drive tissue-scale events.
study_card.expected_result: The tissue carries out fate-driven divisions (>=1) without collapsing (min cells >= initial 4) and conserves particles across splits, so the whole metabolism->fate->division->partition chain composes across all scales.
study_card.main_expert_question: Sustained growth is a tuned regime (target area tracks the metabolite); what growth law would make the non-collapse emergent rather than engineered?
